questions.question: How can you prevent yourself from becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on your driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on your driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, stay calm and focus on your driving. Don't take what other drivers do personally. Plan enough time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: When the driver wears one.
When passengers wear them on long trips.
When everyone wears them on a highway.
When everyone in the car wears them every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: When everyone in the car wears them every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your vehicle should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object and can hurt everyone in the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol over time.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol over time.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to wait for your body to process the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers can help you stay awake, but they cannot lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front of you stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Both directions can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You can only cross these lines to turn left or to safely pass pedestrians, bicyclists, scooter riders, or skateboarders if the opposite lane is clear.

questions.question: When do blind people legally have the right-of-way when crossing the street?

options.text: When wearing light-colored clothing.
When led by a guide dog or using a white or metallic cane.
When helped by another person.
When wearing dark-colored glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: When led by a guide dog or using a white or metallic cane.
questions.explanation: Blind pedestrians using a guide dog or a white or metallic cane have the right-of-way at any crosswalk, even if traffic signals say otherwise.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, roadwork vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. During the day it looks like an orange triangle, and at night it looks like a red triangle.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
They all have air brakes that stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than passenger cars at the same speed. A passenger car going 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio volume.
Park safely and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park safely and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of tiredness while driving: struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting out of your lane, or needing the radio loud to stay awake. If you notice these signs, park in a safe place and take a short nap to refresh yourself.

questions.question: What does a chemical test measure?

options.text: Reaction time.
Blood alcohol content.
Vision.
Driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol content.
questions.explanation: A chemical test measures blood alcohol content (BAC) using breath, blood, urine, or saliva samples. However, a chemical test is not needed to prove intoxication. A police officer's testimony about your driving, appearance, and behavior can be enough evidence for a conviction.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before moving left or right. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before any lane change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Using a hand-held cell phone to talk or listen while driving:

options.text: Is safer than using a hands-free cell phone.
May only be done by teenage drivers.
Is illegal.
Is recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is illegal.
questions.explanation: In New York, it is illegal to hold and use a cell phone while driving. You can use a hand-held phone only to start or end a call. Breaking this law will result in a fine and points on your license.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. You must focus fully on driving. Any other task can be dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following signs is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Regulation signs are white rectangles with black letters or symbols. They provide information about rules, such as speed limits.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Go around them on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the pedestrians have crossed and the intersection is clear before driving.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of both.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs increases how much they impair you. For example, one drink taken with cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. Do not cross if a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous. This applies even if there are no signals or they are not working.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that a lane is ending or the road is narrowing.
